Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. 

It is always a pleasure to work with you, and we are delighted to present our proposal for your component requirements. As a reliable supply partner, we pride ourselves on delivering excellent service and maintaining a comprehensive product range to keep your production running smoothly. 

For the requested volume, we can offer you a price of €5.74 per unit. This quote comes with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net and a contract term of 12 months. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

We trust this proposal meets your expectations and look forward to continuing our successful business relationship. Please do not hesitate to reach out if you have any questions.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Stadler
Inside Sales, Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH

move.subject: Complete fastener kit – bundled supply proposal
move.body:
Dear Mr Stadler,

Thank you for your offer of €5.74 per kit. We would like to build on your existing supply relationship by placing the complete kit with Leitner & Sohn, covering both bolt types, the nuts and the washers.

The enclosed term sheet proposes €5.05 per kit, payment at 90 days net and a contract term of 24 months. It includes a binding commitment of 30000 kits a year throughout the term, representing our full kit requirement. Delivery remains DAP with a lead time of 5 days.

You previously indicated that you could take on additional parts and that the additional shift was on hold. Bundling the complete kit gives you a firm basis for planning that capacity, while giving us a single point of contact for the kit.

What price can you offer against this committed volume and the proposed payment and contract terms?

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Stadler
Inside Sales, Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH

strategy:
P07 — Schraubenhandel Leitner & Sohn GmbH (70610), distributor, Inside Sales Franz Stadler. Bundle the fastener
kit (4 parts: 19 x M12x40 bolt part:360010, 6 x M16x60 bolt part:360011, 21 x M12 nut part:360012, 23 x M12 washer
part:360030) with this one distributor: 30000 kits a year, fixed; lead time 5 days fixed; negotiable: price,
payment days, contract months. Today the parts come from several suppliers; 70610 already delivers three of the
four parts. Its call notes (April/May 2026): "they could take additional parts at short notice; the second shift
has been on hold since spring". Its annual review: price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee.

OBSERVED MECHANIC (34 saved sessions): it opens 5.74 / 30 days / 12 months. First reply is a package answer:
on 90 days / 24 months it goes to 5.59 (sometimes 5.52) whatever we write. It then mirrors our step size, capped
at about 0.10 per reply, and declares a FINAL on its FIFTH reply (5.37-5.42), which we accept. It asks in every
reply "A binding higher volume would help us ... Which volume can you commit to?" and in round 2-3 "Which figures
is that based on? Please send us the data." Nobody ever gave it a NEW verified claim in rounds 2-4 (the saved
sessions re-cited the same forecast and got 'duplicate'). It names PPI-C2594 and LCI-C as cost drivers; both
rose, so there is no index claim - do NOT use index claims. 60 days or 30 days are not worth it (never give
payment days away); 36 months bought nothing; a deep anchor (4.59) drew an early final. Never send 2-3 sheets.

HYPOTHESIS: a NEW verified claim in each of rounds 2, 3 and 4 (forecast, purchase orders, scorecard) plus the same
measured steps makes it step about 0.10 each reply instead of 0.10 / 0.07 / 0.03, so the fifth-reply final lands
at 5.30-5.34 instead of 5.39.

PLAN - always ONE sheet, package S13 (payment 90 days, 24 months). Pick the level whose price is NEAREST the
target price for the round (the menu prices change every round; choose by price, not by level name):
ROUND 1 - target 5.05. Answer its standing question before it asks: the sheet is a binding commitment of 30000
kits a year for the full 24 months (60000 kits), the whole kit from one distributor, kit composition as above; refer
to its own words that it can take additional parts at short notice and that this fills the shift on hold; ask what
price it can offer for this committed kit volume. No claim in round 1 (its first reply is a package answer anyway).
ROUND 2 - target 5.16. Thank it for what it accepted (24 months, 90 days). Answer "which volume": the same 30000
kits a year, binding, 60000 kits over the term - that is the full need. Cite claim fc-latest (our shared forecast
for part:360010, +6.0 %) as the planning basis. Do NOT send the forecast attachment (its per-piece table does not
match kits).
ROUND 3 - target 5.23. Cite the purchase-order claim (po-...: its own delivered price for part:360010 in our
running orders; the claim sentence with the figure is appended by code - do NOT write that price or "per 100" in
your own text, call it "your delivered price for the M12 bolt in our running orders"). Point out the kit moves the
other three parts' volume to it on top of that running business.
ROUND 4 - target 5.27. Cite the scorecard claim (sc-...: its on-time delivery 88.6 %) neutrally: we are
consolidating on it despite that figure because of its range and short notice capacity; ask for its best price on
this committed package.
ROUND 5 - target 5.31, no new claim, ask for its best price. Code accepts when it agrees or goes final; never argue
with a final offer.
Tone: courteous, concrete, short (600-1000 characters before the claim lines). Never mention a committee, a
deadline, our other suppliers' prices, or urgency. Do not repeat a claim already sent. Each round: one new
element, answer every question it asked, describe exactly the one sheet you send.
